title: Bun Bo Xao
subtitle: Vietnamese stir-fried beef vermicelli. 10 min prep, 10 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Ask Tops/Villa butcher for shabu-shabu cut — already thin. Or freeze 20 min and slice yourself.
Dry rice vermicelli (sen mee) — same as Thai sen mee, packaged labelled 'rice vermicelli'.

ingredients.note: Oil cap. For searing the beef hot and fast.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Use only the bottom 4cm tender core. The rest goes in the freezer for stock.

ingredients.note: Generous handful — this is the Vietnamese soul.

substitutions.note: Leaner, higher protein. Marinate the same way.
Drops kcal by ~200 / carbs by ~45g. Texture goes spongier.

steps.text: Soak rice vermicelli in just-boiled water 5 min, then drain and rinse cold. Divide into 2 bowls.
Marinate beef with half the fish sauce, soy, sugar, minced lemongrass, half the garlic. Sit 5 min.
Whisk remaining fish sauce, lime juice, 2 tbsp water, sugar, chili, remaining garlic — this is the nuoc cham. Set aside.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a wok screaming hot. Sear beef in two batches 90 sec each — don't crowd. Just-cooked-through.
Build bowls: vermicelli base, bean sprouts and cucumber on the side, beef on top.
Drown in nuoc cham (use it all). Shower mint, cilantro, crushed peanuts. Toss together at the table.

notes: Bun bo xao is the Vietnamese answer to a salad-bowl meal — cold noodles, hot beef, raw herbs, sour-sweet-salty dressing pulling it together. Two key moves: sear the beef HARD and FAST (cold pan = grey meat), and don't skimp on mint. Bean sprouts must be raw.
